clips.title: The state of the art in tackling Flaky Tests
clips.why: What happens to a team when flaky tests are ignored: people stop trusting red, which is exactly where fcp's nightly is.
look: Ignoring flaky tests: the cost is not the one test, it is that every red result loses its meaning.
The psychological barrier: once people expect red, they stop looking.
Why the fix starts with measuring, not with retries.
clips.after: Sixty red nights in a row is that barrier; the per-test history is the measurement.

clips.title: Test quarantine or how to manage flaky tests — Ivan Varivoda, Wrike
clips.why: A real team's test quarantine: flaky tests keep running in their own place, so they stop blocking everyone while someone fixes them.
look: How a test enters quarantine and who decides.
Quarantined tests still run, so the team can see when they are fixed.
Why every quarantined test needs an owner, or quarantine becomes a graveyard.
clips.after: Our quarantine marker works the same way: the test runs every night, the night stays green, and a flaky-test ticket names the owner.

practice.q: Finish the line in conftest.py that turns a quarantine into an expected failure that still runs.
practice.hint: Should a pass of a quarantined test be an error?
practice.why: Non-strict means a pass is fine. A flaky test passes most nights, and a strict xfail would turn every good night red.

practice.q: The nightly's tests run inside a Kubernetes pod through kubectl exec. Where must the step that copies junit.xml out go?

options.text: After the step that deletes the pod, so the pod is clean.
options.why: The file lives inside the pod, so it is gone once the pod is deleted.

options.text: Before the step that deletes the pod, with if: always().
options.why: The report is most needed on failing nights, and it must leave the pod before the pod is removed.

options.text: Anywhere, because pytest uploads the file to GitHub by itself.
options.why: pytest only writes a file. Uploading it as an artifact is a separate step.

practice.q: Put one triage of a scattered-red test in order.
items: The history table shows test_run_report red on nights 1, 2 and 10 only
The BE guild calls it flaky and names an owner
A person opens a flaky-test ticket, RH-1251
A person adds @pytest.mark.quarantine(ticket="RH-1251") to the test
The flaky-test fixer works on the ticket while the test keeps running every night
practice.why: Measure first, decide with people, give it a ticket and an owner, and keep it running so the fix can be seen.

practice.q: On night 5, twenty tests in many different areas fail at once, and on night 6 they all pass again. Which category fits first?

options.text: Environment: something in QA broke for one night.
options.why: One red column across many unrelated tests points at the environment. Hand it to DevOps with the evidence.

options.text: Twenty flaky tests, so quarantine them all.
options.why: Twenty independent flaky tests failing on the same night is very unlikely. Quarantining them would hide a real problem.

options.text: A regression from a change merged before night 5.
options.why: A regression would stay red on night 6 too, unless someone reverted the change.
